rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Evidence: the course is about 4 to 5 m and must be covered in under 3 s (about 1.5 m/s average), so the baseline needs a base_speed near 1.5 to 1.6 and a wheel radius that gives usable ground speed. Geometry: five sensors spaced 2 cm apart across the front of the axle (x = +0.04 to -0.04, y = 0.03), with a 12 mm footprint. Five sensors cover the 25 mm tape with overlap, so the line stays visible through the bends. Sensor weights are +2, +1, 0, -1, -2, matching the sign convention (positive x is left, positive signal steers left). kp = 2 gives a moderate steering response, since the 350 PWM per turn unit scale could oscillate at higher gains. kd = 0.05 damps the response without amplifying sensor noise. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on the bends. line_loss = last_direction recovers toward the side where the line was last seen. Expected result: the robot completes most of the oval and s-bend at around 1.5 m/s with a modest rms_error. The main risks are oscillation on the slalom (kp too high) and loss of the line on tight bends (speed too high). The observation request is set to measure these two directly. Next-iteration hypotheses: if steering_oscillation is high, reduce kp or raise kd; if line_loss_events is nonzero, lower base_speed or widen the sensor spread; if completion_time is above 3 s, raise base_speed.
